cover.sub: Evidence-led direction across six priorities for Eneus and its agency partners.
cover.prepared: Prepared for Eneus Energy by FatCat9
cover.notes: Cover. Period covered: 1 July 2025 to 30 October 2026, observed online conversation about the proposed Hunterston Data Centre in North Ayrshire.

contents.title: Start with the overview
contents.sub: The opening sections explain how the recommendations were developed, what requires attention and the direction proposed.
overview: The evidence, opportunity and method behind the recommendations.
What the public conversation indicates requires attention.

method.title: From evidence to
method.sub: The recommendations combine observed conversation patterns, project evidence and communication opportunity to define a focused direction for each priority.
steps: Use recurring concerns, action patterns, publisher behaviour and qualitative examples to define the communication problem—not assumptions.
IDENTIFY WHERE COMMUNICATION CAN MAKE A DIFFERENCE
Prioritise opportunities to improve understanding, credibility or action; recognise where evidence, policy or delivery—not communication—is the constraint.
BUILD A TAILORED PLAN FOR EACH PRIORITY
Set the recommended shift, possible actions, priority stakeholders, credibility conditions, watchouts and activation signals.

priorities.title: Six priorities
priorities.sub: Each priority addresses a distinct communication challenge; together they form one integrated direction for the project.
priorities.note: Concern percentages show the share of 302 project publications mentioning each theme; themes overlap. Wider context uses 409 publications. Priority 6 shows publisher and statement patterns.
cols: Strongest local reaction; most likely to move into collective action.
Trust depends on visible questions and decisions after consultation.
Risk rises when current, site-specific evidence is unavailable.
Wider debate cannot be resolved by project information alone.
Positive foundation; credibility requires demonstrable local delivery.
Evidence must travel through credible intermediaries.

exec.title: Six priorities.
exec.sub: Each priority defines the most important communication shift required to make the project easier to evaluate.
common: Build one current project record that decision-relevant audiences can inspect, verify and use—without overstating what is known.
cols: Make the Port site the project story.
Start with the confirmed project and current evidence; acknowledge the move without making it the organising frame.
Show the chain from question to status, evidence and decision—including what changed, what did not and why.
Let confidence rise with the evidence.
Distinguish facts, assumptions, assessments and commitments; show the source, limits, relevance and next update.
Keep Hunterston facts, planning decisions and national policy questions separate.
Replace broad benefit claims with visible supplier routes and projected, contracted and delivered results.
Start with the decision, audience and evidence need; then choose the intermediary, outlet, platform and format.

opener.title: The Port Site Creates a Stronger Opening—But Not a Blank Slate
opener.sub: Landscape, heritage and biodiversity remain strategically important; their relevance and treatment should now be determined by the conditions of the Port site.
opener.signalsLabel: SHARE OF PROJECT PUBLICATIONS MENTIONING EACH THEME

shift.title: Make the Port Site the Story—Not the Move
shift.sub: The initial framing will influence whether audiences evaluate the current project or debate why the location changed.
shift.estLead: The previous location became part of the argument against the project.
est: Place-specific features made opposition easy to visualise.
Campaign claims travelled into media and political channels.
Collective action is already framed as effective.
Economic arguments did not displace location-based concerns.
shift.shiftLead: Introduce the project through the confirmed Port site—not through the decision to move.
shifts: Lead with what the project is now: its location, status, confirmed parameters and current evidence.
Treat the location change as a factual project update, not as the central narrative.
Avoid direct comparisons or language such as better, improved or corrected.
Carry forward only the place-related issues that remain relevant to the Port site.
Address questions about the former site briefly and factually when they arise.
shift.key: Acknowledge the location change clearly, but keep the confirmed project—not the relocation—as the organising frame.

actions.title: Build the Current Project Record Before Others Define the Move
actions.sub: Four coordinated actions to make the Port-site project—not the move—the usable public reference.
actions.rule: Lead with the current Port-site record. Refer to the former site only when directly relevant, using one brief, agreed factual statement—without comparison or retrospective justification.
rows: INTRODUCE SITE + EVIDENCE TOGETHER
Make the Port site the first complete project record audiences encounter.
Release the site map, status, confirmed parameters and evidence links together through the project page and factual brief.
RESET THE EVIDENCE SYSTEM
Stop legacy assets or unsupported site claims from circulating as current.
Classify live assets as current, update, redirect, archive or withdraw; record evidence, owner and permitted use for location-dependent claims.
REASSESS PLACE-RELATED THEMES
Carry forward only place issues that materially affect the Port-site case.
Assign landscape, heritage and biodiversity to lead evidence, supporting Q&A or retire; surface only what remains decision-relevant.
MAKE OPPORTUNITY TANGIBLE
Turn economic opportunity into a credible route to participation.
Confirm prior-site figures before reuse; distinguish demand from commitment and show supplier access and timing.

stake.title: Equip Four Audience Groups to Evaluate, Validate and Carry the Port-Site Case
stake.sub: Focus on audiences who can decide, test or explain—not on converting committed opponents.
stake.std: One shared project record, adapted by audience: current facts, evidence status, source access, and clear boundaries between confirmed facts, expectations and commitments.
rows: PLANNING AUTHORITIES & STATUTORY CONSULTEES
EVALUATE
Site-specific evidence organised around statutory remit, consent stage, open technical questions and next decisions.
POLITICAL & CIVIC DECISION-MAKERS
INTERPRET & EXPLAIN
An attributable brief on local implications, current status, confirmed facts, open issues and the next milestone.
TECHNICAL & DELIVERY VALIDATORS
TEST & VALIDATE
Evidence, methods, assumptions and responsible sources they can independently examine—without being asked to endorse.
MEDIA, BUSINESS BODIES & CREDIBLE INTERMEDIARIES
CARRY & SHARE
Current visuals, attributable facts, concise Q&A and direct source links that can be accurately cited and shared.
bar: Make accurate evidence easy to reuse in each audience’s own voice.

watch.title: Five Ways the Story Could Work Against the Project
watch.sub: Each risk is triggered by a plausible communications choice—not by opposition alone.
risks: VICTORY FRAME
If the move leads the story
Lead with the current project and evidence—not campaign reaction.
RETROSPECTIVE ADMISSION
If the new site is called “better”
Avoid direct comparison that reopens the case for the former site.
OLD CONCERNS, NEW SITE
If every previous issue is repeated
Address only concerns that current evidence shows remain relevant.
OPPORTUNITY BECOMES PROMISE
If potential benefits sound guaranteed
Separate expected activity, opportunity and confirmed commitment.
INTEREST BECOMES SUPPORT
If participation is treated as endorsement
Keep business interest, validation and community support distinct.
watch.implication: Use the confirmed site as the organising frame; treat the former site only as necessary historical context.

act.title: Territory 1 Activation Plan: Sequence and Signals of Progress
act.sub: A staged approach to establish the current Port-site project as the basis for evaluation and identify where further communications support is needed.
seq: Establish the current project
Introduce one complete Port-site record and treat the location change as a factual update.
Equip consequential audiences
Provide role-specific evidence that can be verified, cited and shared.
Reinforce selectively
Address genuine evidence gaps without reopening former-site issues that are no longer relevant.
prog: Current Port-site facts become the default reference.
Influential audiences reuse current evidence—not campaign interpretations.
Relocation is treated as a project update, not as victory or retrospective admission.
Opportunities remain distinct from commitments, and former-site material no longer shapes interpretation.
act.footer: The subsequent playbook will translate these findings into platform, voice, format and agency-activation choices.

opener.title: Consultation Was a Moment; Trust Depends on What Remains Visible Afterwards
opener.sub: Criticism focused on access, clarity, unanswered questions and whether participation affected the project—not simply on whether consultation occurred.
opener.signalsLabel: DIAGNOSTIC SIGNALS: THEME PRESENCE AND CONSULTATION TIMING

shift.title: Move From Consultation Events to a Traceable Decision Record
shift.sub: Trust depends less on how much engagement occurred than on whether people can see what was heard, answered and changed.
shift.estLead: The consultation created activity—but not a durable public record.
est: Timing and accessibility became part of the criticism.
Attendees described unclear answers and limited local knowledge.
A postponed event reinforced doubts about process reliability.
Eneus said feedback was shaping the project, but changes were not visible in the observed record.
shift.shiftLead: Treat consultation as a visible chain: question → status → evidence → decision or change.
shifts: State what participants can influence and what is fixed.
Publish material questions, responsible owner and response status.
Show what changed, what did not and why.
Distinguish information events, dialogue and statutory consultation.
Carry forward only feedback still relevant to the Port site.
shift.key: Do not ask audiences to trust the process; make the process inspectable.

actions.title: Make Consultation Produce a Public Record—Not Another Event
actions.sub: Four actions can turn participation into traceable evidence without promising agreement.
actions.rule: Evidence of listening is not attendance; it is a visible record of what was raised, how it was handled and what follows.
rows: PUBLISH QUESTION + STATUS LOG
Stop recurring issues from disappearing after events.
Group recurring questions; mark answered, evidence pending, outside scope or decision required; link the source and update date.
SHOW FEEDBACK → DECISION
Demonstrate where participation affected the project.
Record feedback, response, decision and rationale; state “no change” with reasons when applicable.
LABEL THE PROCESS
Prevent information sessions from being read as consultation or attendance as consent.
Label each activity: inform, listen, validate or statutory consultation; state what can change and who decides.
CARRY FORWARD VALID INPUT
Respect earlier participation without importing obsolete site issues.
Map prior feedback as still relevant, re-evaluate or retire; explain only material carry-forward decisions.

stake.title: Make the Process Usable to Four Audiences—Not Simply Visible
stake.sub: Trust improves when each audience knows what it can influence, who answers and where the outcome will be recorded.
stake.std: Every engagement should state its purpose, scope, decision owner, evidence status and next visible update.
rows: COMMUNITY COUNCILS & LOCAL PARTICIPANTS
RAISE & TRACK
A question-and-status record showing the responsible source, next step and whether the issue remains relevant to the Port site.
PLANNING AUTHORITIES & STATUTORY CONSULTEES
TEST & DECIDE
Complete evidence, consultation record, unresolved issues and a traceable route from feedback to decision.
ELECTED REPRESENTATIVES
SCRUTINISE & EXPLAIN
A concise verified brief: material questions, current answers, project changes and the next decision milestone.
MEDIA & COMMUNITY INTERMEDIARIES
VERIFY & CARRY
Linkable Q&A, response status, dates, sources and corrections that can be checked and shared accurately.
bar: Credibility comes from traceability, not from asking audiences to trust the process.

watch.title: Five Ways Consultation Can Deepen Distrust
watch.sub: The risk is not disagreement; it is creating evidence that participation is symbolic, selective or impossible to verify.
risks: ATTENDANCE = ACCEPTANCE
If turnout or silence is read as consent
Report participation neutrally; never infer support from attendance or absence.
LISTENING WITHOUT TRACE
If feedback disappears after the event
Publish the status and outcome of material questions.
INFORMATION AS CONSULTATION
If presenting information is described as influence
State what can change, what cannot and who decides.
REASSURANCE BEFORE EVIDENCE
If uncertainty is filled with confident claims
Mark evidence pending and name the source and next update.
PROCESS RESET
If relocation erases earlier participation
Carry forward relevant input and retire obsolete issues explicitly.
watch.implication: Treat consultation as a decision record—not a volume of activity.

act.title: Territory 2 Activation Plan: Build the Record, Then Demonstrate Its Use
act.sub: A staged approach to make participation traceable and show whether questions are producing visible answers, decisions or changes.
seq: Establish the baseline
Consolidate material questions and status; distinguish current from former-site issues.
Close the loop
Add evidence, decision or rationale and the next visible step.
Engage selectively
Use future dialogue only where it can resolve a defined issue or influence a decision.
prog: People can find response status without attending an event.
Repeated questions point to the same current answer and source.
Project changes and no-change decisions are visible with reasons.
Attendance, silence and participation are not presented as support.
act.footer: The subsequent playbook will translate these conditions into platform, voice, format and agency-activation choices.

opener.title: Biodiversity Draws Reaction; Technical Claims Need Verifiable Evidence
opener.sub: Biodiversity is both a local concern and an evidence test; energy, planning, water and flooding require current, site-specific proof.
opener.signalsLabel: DIAGNOSTIC SIGNALS: SHARE OF PROJECT PUBLICATIONS MENTIONING EACH THEME · THEMES OVERLAP

shift.title: Move From Technical Reassurance to a Visible Evidence Ladder
shift.sub: Credibility depends on showing what is confirmed, what is still being assessed and who is responsible for each conclusion.
shift.estLead: Technical concerns do not all carry the same evidence status—or the same communication risk.
est: Biodiversity generates visible reaction and connects to local identity.
Energy, planning, water and flooding produce factual questions.
Eneus has published water information, while ecology remains under assessment.
Flooding has little volume but can carry high local and regulatory consequence.
shift.shiftLead: Make evidence maturity part of the communication—not something hidden behind confident language.
shifts: For every material impact, show the claim, source, status, owner and next update.
Separate confirmed facts, design assumptions, assessments and commitments.
Use plain-English summaries that link to the underlying evidence.
State uncertainty and current-site applicability explicitly.
Let technical confidence rise only as the evidence does.
shift.key: A visible evidence gap is manageable; an overstated claim can become a credibility problem.

actions.title: Build a Technical Evidence System—Not a Collection of Reassurances
actions.sub: Four practical actions can make technical claims current, attributable and usable without overstating certainty.
actions.rule: Every material technical claim should reveal its current-site source, evidence status, responsible owner and next update.
rows: BUILD AN IMPACT EVIDENCE REGISTER
Prevent contradictory, obsolete or unsupported claims from circulating.
Record issue, public claim, current-site evidence, method, owner, status, uncertainty, publication date and next material update.
CLASSIFY EVIDENCE STATUS
Separate what is known from what remains under development.
Label each claim: confirmed fact, design assumption, assessment underway or commitment; never blend categories.
PUBLISH USABLE SUMMARIES
Make technical evidence understandable without removing its limits.
For priority issues, state the question, finding, method, limitations, current-site relevance and link to the full source.
ROUTE CLAIMS TO THE RIGHT SOURCE
Give high-consequence claims the correct authority without implying endorsement.
Attribute water, flooding, ecology, energy and planning evidence to its responsible source; state exactly what was verified.

stake.title: Let the Right Institutions Carry the Right Kind of Technical Credibility
stake.sub: Different audiences need different levels of evidence—but all should trace back to the same current source.
stake.std: Every technical claim should show source, method, evidence status, current-site applicability, owner and date.
rows: PLANNING AUTHORITIES & STATUTORY CONSULTEES
TEST & DECIDE
Full assessments, assumptions, unresolved issues and relevance to planning or consent.
TECHNICAL AUTHORS, UTILITIES & VALIDATORS
VERIFY THE SOURCE
Source data, methodology, scope and a precise statement of what they have—and have not—verified.
ELECTED & COMMUNITY REPRESENTATIVES
INTERPRET & SCRUTINISE
Plain-English impact briefs, maps, evidence status, material uncertainties and the next decision point.
MEDIA & COMMUNITY INTERMEDIARIES
CARRY ACCURATELY
Attributable facts, source links, simple diagrams and a clear route for technical corrections.
bar: Credibility increases when audiences can see what is known, what is pending and who owns the answer.

watch.title: Five Ways Technical Communication Can Create More Risk
watch.sub: The danger is not uncertainty itself; it is allowing assumptions, obsolete evidence or third-party authority to imply more certainty than exists.
risks: OLD SITE, NEW CLAIM
If former-site evidence travels with the relocated project
Use it only after confirming and labelling its relevance to the Port site.
ASSUMPTION BECOMES FACT
If a design estimate is repeated as a confirmed outcome
Show the evidence category and the condition required for confirmation.
VALIDATOR BECOMES ENDORSER
If a utility or consultant reference implies project approval
State exactly what was verified—and what was not.
LOW VOLUME = LOW RISK
If flooding is deprioritised because few publications mention it
Prioritise by consequence and regulatory relevance, not conversation volume alone.
REPORT WITHOUT INTERPRETATION
If evidence is published without relevance, limits or context
Pair the source with a plain-English summary and explicit limitations.
watch.implication: Technical confidence should rise only as the evidence matures; communication should show that progression.

act.title: Territory 3 Activation Plan: Establish the Evidence Base, Then Make It Usable
act.sub: A staged approach to align technical claims with current-site evidence and make the strongest available proof easy to verify.
seq: Establish the baseline
Inventory public technical claims; assign current-site status, owner and evidence source.
Release by decision relevance
Prioritise planning/EIA and biodiversity; publish energy, water and flooding when evidence reaches a usable threshold.
Equip others to use it
Provide source-linked briefs, maps and Q&A for validators, representatives and media.
prog: Eneus and its agencies use the same current source.
Confirmed facts, assumptions, assessments and commitments remain distinct.
Each material claim has a named source, date and current-site applicability.
Former-site evidence is not presented as current without explicit validation.
act.footer: The subsequent playbook will translate these conditions into platform, voice, format and agency-activation choices.

opener.title: National Policy Gives Local Opposition a Route Into Scottish Politics
opener.sub: AI policy is a project concern, but the moratorium and regulation debate is much larger than Hunterston—and cannot be answered by Eneus alone.
opener.signalsLabel: DIAGNOSTIC SIGNALS: PROJECT PRESENCE, NATIONAL SCALE AND ACTION LINK

shift.title: Move From Defending the Sector to Defining the Project Boundary
shift.sub: Eneus can clarify Hunterston and its compliance position without attempting to settle Scotland’s wider debate about AI or data-centre policy.
shift.estLead: Hunterston is being used as an example inside a much larger policy dispute.
est: AI policy is 13% of the project debate, but 45% of the Scottish debate.
Moratorium calls connect local campaigns with MSPs and national media.
Questions extend to cumulative energy, water, planning and the need for AI infrastructure.
Eneus does not control national policy or sector-wide impacts.
shift.shiftLead: Answer the Hunterston question clearly; locate the policy question with the institution that owns it.
shifts: Define what Eneus controls, what the consent process decides and what government policy determines.
Translate policy changes into project implications without turning communication into lobbying.
Publish project facts relevant to national questions; do not speak for the entire sector.
Update the position at material policy or decision points.
Keep local evidence and national arguments analytically separate.
shift.key: Silence allows conflation; overreach turns Eneus into the defender of the whole sector.

actions.title: Create a Clear Boundary Between Project Facts and National Policy
actions.sub: Four actions can keep Hunterston legible while Scotland’s policy framework continues to evolve.
actions.rule: Every policy statement should separate project fact, planning requirement and national policy question.
rows: PUBLISH A POLICY BOUNDARY
Prevent Hunterston from absorbing responsibility for the wider debate.
Show three columns: what Hunterston controls, what planning and consent decide, and what Scottish or UK policy determines.
TRANSLATE POLICY INTO PROJECT EFFECT
Show what a policy or guidance change actually means for Hunterston.
State applicability, project dependency, current stage and the next formal decision whenever guidance changes.
CREATE A PROJECT FACT BRIEF
Answer national questions with bounded project evidence.
Cover site demand, energy, water, EIA and cumulative-impact relevance; link sources and state the limits.
ROUTE QUESTIONS BY RESPONSIBLE OWNER
Reduce speculation and contradictory answers.
Assign questions to Eneus, the planning authority, government, utilities or another owner; state when Eneus cannot answer.

stake.title: Give Each Policy Audience the Evidence It Can Actually Use
stake.sub: Credibility comes from giving each audience the project facts and policy context relevant to its role—without asking it to validate the project.
stake.std: Use one boundary across all materials: project fact, planning implication, policy question and responsible institution.
rows: SCOTTISH GOVERNMENT & POLICY OFFICIALS
SET POLICY
Current project facts, evidence dependencies and the practical implications of emerging policy.
PLANNING AUTHORITY & STATUTORY CONSULTEES
APPLY & DECIDE
Applicable guidance, consent requirements, evidence status and unresolved dependencies.
MSPs & ELECTED REPRESENTATIVES
SCRUTINISE & EXPLAIN
A concise separation of Hunterston facts, national questions and the next formal decision.
POLICY & MEDIA INTERMEDIARIES
INTERPRET ACCURATELY
An attributable current position, links to official guidance and clear limits on what Eneus can answer.
bar: Eneus gains credibility by being precise about what it can answer and what it cannot.

watch.title: Five Ways the National Debate Can Pull the Project Off Course
watch.sub: The risk is not policy criticism; it is allowing Hunterston to become a proxy for every unresolved question about AI and data centres.
risks: PROJECT = SECTOR
If Eneus tries to defend data centres or AI overall
Speak for Hunterston and its evidence—not for the entire industry.
POLICY AS AN OBSTACLE
If guidance or a pause is framed as a hurdle to defeat
Describe the decision framework and its project implications neutrally.
CERTAINTY BEFORE GUIDANCE
If compliance or outcomes are claimed while policy is evolving
State current status, dependencies and what remains undecided.
LOCAL FACTS = NATIONAL PROOF
If Hunterston evidence is used to answer cumulative national impacts
Separate project-level evidence from system-level questions.
NO PROJECT POSITION
If silence lets others define Hunterston’s relationship to policy
Publish a bounded factual position at material policy moments.
watch.implication: Own the project boundary; do not inherit responsibility for the entire national debate.

act.title: Territory 4 Activation Plan: Define the Boundary, Then Update at Decision Moments
act.sub: A staged approach to keep the project legible while national policy and planning guidance continue to evolve.
seq: Establish the boundary
Agree what Eneus can answer, what planning determines and what policy institutions own.
Translate material change
Update only when guidance, EIA rules, application status or government position changes.
Equip decision-relevant audiences
Use a policy brief and project fact sheet with direct source links, not broad sector commentary.
prog: Coverage distinguishes Hunterston facts from the national debate.
Project statements show the current policy status and date.
No claim implies Eneus can determine national need or cumulative impacts.
Policy questions are consistently routed to the responsible institution.
act.footer: The subsequent playbook will translate these conditions into platform, voice, format and agency-activation choices.

opener.title: The Positive Case Is Small—but It Reveals What Must Become Tangible
opener.sub: Observed support is narrow and business-led. It centres on supplier access, jobs and regional value—not broad enthusiasm for the project.
opener.signalsLabel: DIAGNOSTIC SIGNALS: OBSERVED SUPPORT AND ECONOMIC THEME PRESENCE

shift.title: Move From Economic Promise to a Verifiable Local Value Proposition
shift.sub: Investment becomes persuasive only when audiences can see who can participate, where value lands, when it occurs and what Eneus can genuinely commit.
shift.estLead: The positive case exists, but it is conditional and easy to challenge.
est: Explicit support is 2.3% and is concentrated in the business ecosystem.
Supplier opportunity is the clearest external positive signal.
Employment is mentioned in 10%, but job claims are contested on scale and permanence.
Capital investment does not automatically become local value.
shift.shiftLead: Communicate economic value as a delivery mechanism—not as a headline number.
shifts: Define the geography and categories included in “local value.”
Separate projected, targeted, contracted and delivered value.
Show the route, timing and requirements for supplier participation.
Connect commitments to procurement and skills partners.
Publish results only when they can be verified.
shift.key: A smaller defensible claim is more valuable than a large number that cannot yet be traced to local delivery.

actions.title: Turn Economic Potential Into a Route People Can See and Use
actions.sub: Four actions can move the positive case from potential benefit to measurable local participation.
actions.rule: No economic claim should appear without a geography, value category, delivery status and evidence source.
rows: DEFINE A LOCAL VALUE BASELINE
Make “local” and “value” measurable before promoting either.
Define North Ayrshire, Ayrshire and Scotland separately; specify jobs, supplier spend, contracts, training and relevant exclusions.
CREATE A COMMITMENT LADDER
Prevent projections from being read as promises or outcomes.
Label each claim as projection, target, procurement requirement, contracted value or delivered result.
BUILD A SUPPLIER ACCESS PATH
Turn general opportunity into a practical route to participate.
Show work packages, timing, qualification criteria, registration route, contact and expected decision point.
PUBLISH A LOCAL VALUE LEDGER
Make delivery visible at the moments when evidence exists.
At procurement milestones, report opportunities issued, awards, spend, jobs and training with dates and denominators.

stake.title: Build the Positive Case With the Actors Who Can Turn It Into Delivery
stake.sub: Economic credibility depends on linking opportunity, capability, procurement and public reporting—not on asking third parties to repeat benefit claims.
stake.std: Every economic claim should state geography, type of value, time horizon, delivery status, owner and evidence.
rows: LOCAL BUSINESSES & SUPPLIER NETWORKS
PREPARE & BID
Visible work packages, timelines, qualification requirements, registration and procurement contacts.
ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, SKILLS & COLLEGES
ALIGN CAPABILITY
Workforce baseline, capability gaps, realistic training pathways and evidence of demand.
DELIVERY & PROCUREMENT PARTNERS
CONVERT TO CONTRACT
Measurable local-value requirements, tender mechanisms, reporting fields and delivery ownership.
ELECTED, COMMUNITY & MEDIA INTERMEDIARIES
SCRUTINISE BENEFIT
Clear definitions, current status, local outcomes and the limits of what is not yet known.
bar: Support grows from visible participation and delivery, not from repeating the scale of investment.

watch.title: Five Ways Economic Communication Can Undermine the Positive Case
watch.sub: The risk is not modest evidence; it is allowing projections, interest or investment scale to imply local benefits that have not yet been secured.
risks: INVESTMENT = LOCAL BENEFIT
If total capital value is presented as value retained locally
Show the mechanism and share that could realistically enter the local economy.
CONSTRUCTION = PERMANENT
If temporary and operational employment are blended
Separate job type, duration, timing and evidence status.
“LOCAL” WITHOUT A MAP
If Ayrshire, North Ayrshire and Scotland are used interchangeably
Define the geography for every target and result.
INTEREST = DELIVERY
If event attendance or supplier registration is presented as benefit
Report contracts, spend and jobs separately from expressions of interest.
TARGET WITHOUT A MECHANISM
If a local-value ambition is detached from procurement
Connect it to tender criteria, ownership and reporting.
watch.implication: Economic communication should never run ahead of procurement and delivery evidence.

act.title: Territory 5 Activation Plan: Define Value Before Promoting It
act.sub: A staged approach to make economic claims more credible as design, procurement and delivery become more concrete.
seq: Establish definitions
Set geographies, value categories, baseline, status labels and reporting ownership.
Connect claims to delivery
Translate targets into supplier packages, procurement requirements and skills pathways.
Report at evidence milestones
Publish contracted and delivered results separately from projections and expressions of interest.
prog: Every claim identifies geography, type, timing and status.
Suppliers can see a credible route from interest to procurement.
Targets are traceable to delivery requirements and owners.
Published results distinguish projected, contracted and delivered value.
act.footer: The subsequent playbook will translate these conditions into platform, voice, format and agency-activation choices.

opener.title: Eneus Does Not Need More Volume—Its Evidence Needs to Travel Better
opener.sub: Community and individuals originate much of the volume; media extend it; Eneus explanations mainly appear through other publishers.
opener.signalsLabel: DIAGNOSTIC SIGNALS: WHO PUBLISHES AND HOW ENEUS INFORMATION CIRCULATES

shift.title: Move From More Visibility to Deliberate Information Pathways
shift.sub: The goal is not maximum publication volume; it is to get decision-relevant evidence to the people who can use, test or carry it accurately.
shift.estLead: The conversation is distributed, but visibility and influence are concentrated.
est: Community groups and individuals publish 51% of the conversation.
One campaign produces 24% of all publications and 33% of recorded interactions.
Media publish 37% and carry issues into the public record.
Eneus authors under 1%; its statements appear in 23%, mainly through others.
shift.shiftLead: Build an evidence route for each decision—not a generic distribution list.
shifts: Identify the decision audience, credible intermediary and evidence needed.
Use a stable Eneus source as the anchor; tailored materials should point back to it.
Prioritise decision relevance, subject authority, trust and correction behaviour.
Use third parties within their expertise without implying endorsement.
Let the playbook specify the platform, outlet, voice and format for each route.
shift.key: Campaign volume is a visibility fact—not a reason to let the campaign choose every communication priority.

actions.title: Design the Route Evidence Must Travel Before Choosing the Channel
actions.sub: Four actions can connect priority evidence to the audiences and intermediaries most relevant to decisions.
actions.rule: Every distribution choice should name the decision audience, evidence need, intermediary role and source of truth.
rows: MAP INFLUENCE PATHWAYS
Direct evidence toward actors with genuine decision impact.
For each decision, map audience → intermediary → evidence → channel → responsible owner.
BUILD ROLE-SPECIFIC SOURCE PACKAGES
Avoid forcing one press release or Q&A to serve every audience.
Create modular materials for planning, technical evidence, local process and economic value, each linked to the source.
USE HUB + SPOKE DISTRIBUTION
Let information travel without losing attribution or status.
Keep a stable Eneus source; agencies and intermediaries can add context but should link back and retain dates.
SET INTERMEDIARY SELECTION CRITERIA
Choose credibility and relevance before audience size.
Assess decision relevance, subject authority, audience trust, accuracy and correction behaviour; treat follower count as secondary.

stake.title: Use Different Networks for Decisions, Interpretation and Credibility
stake.sub: The same evidence should travel differently depending on whether an audience decides, verifies, interprets or carries it.
stake.std: Every material should retain the source, evidence status, date, owner and a route for correction.
rows: PLANNING & POLICY DECISION-MAKERS
DECIDE & SCRUTINISE
Direct, current evidence tied to the decision, statutory process and unresolved dependencies.
LOCAL & REGIONAL MEDIA
VERIFY & FRAME
Attributable facts, usable context, source links, deadlines and a clear correction route.
COMMUNITY COUNCILS & CIVIC NETWORKS
INTERPRET LOCALLY
Local relevance, open issues, decision points and materials they can interpret without being treated as endorsers.
TECHNICAL & ECONOMIC VALIDATORS
CARRY WITHIN EXPERTISE
Bounded claims within their expertise and a precise statement of what they have—and have not—verified.
bar: Success means evidence remains traceable and usable as it moves through others.

watch.title: Five Ways Distribution Can Distort the Evidence
watch.sub: The risk is not using third parties; it is confusing visibility with influence or allowing evidence to lose its source, status or limits as it travels.
risks: REACH = INFLUENCE
If audience size is treated as decision impact
Prioritise the pathway to the decision, not the largest visible channel.
INTERMEDIARY = ENDORSER
If carrying information is interpreted as project support
State the intermediary’s role and never imply endorsement.
ONE PACKAGE FOR ALL
If every audience receives the same material
Adapt the entry point while preserving the underlying source.
CAMPAIGN SETS THE AGENDA
If campaign volume determines every communication priority
Prioritise by decision consequence, evidence need and strategic territory.
SOURCE LOST IN TRANSIT
If a claim circulates without its date, status or evidence link
Design every derivative item to point back to the current source.
watch.implication: Design distribution around decisions and evidence integrity—not publication volume.

act.title: Territory 6 Activation Plan: Build the Route Before Choosing the Channel
act.sub: A staged approach to connect each decision-relevant audience with the evidence and intermediary it can use most credibly.
seq: Map decision paths
Identify the decision, actor, evidence need, credible intermediary and responsible owner.
Prepare source packages
Create one current evidence hub with role-specific entry points and links back.
Activate in sequence
Reach decision-makers and validators first, then media and community networks with usable context.
prog: Decision-relevant audiences receive evidence before material moments.
Third-party materials trace back to the same current source.
Intermediaries retain claim status, limitations and attribution.
Agencies can identify which pathway each platform, outlet, voice and format serves.
act.footer: The playbook will name the specific platforms, outlets, voices and formats for each information pathway.
